title: Mentorship & Coaching for New Instructors
contentStatus: Draft for DiFacto review. Title and content to be confirmed.

sections.title: Why Mentorship Is Separate from Teaching Skill
learningObjectives: Understand the distinction between delivering training and mentoring a new instructor
Recognize why this is treated as its own competency area
sections.content: L5-M1 built the skill of teaching a session well. This module addresses something different: supporting another person as they become an instructor themselves. A Master Instructor who teaches excellently doesn't automatically know how to mentor someone else through that same development - mentorship is an ongoing, relational skill, not a one-time delivery skill.

keyTerms.note: An ongoing supportive relationship in which an experienced instructor helps a newer one develop.

sections.title: What New Instructors Actually Struggle With
learningObjectives: Understand common early struggles for newly certified instructors
Recognize how this differs from struggles a learner has with technical content
sections.content: New instructors often know the technical material well - they passed their own certification - but struggle with the instructional side: managing a room, adjusting pace in real time, or handling a question they didn't anticipate. These are confidence and experience gaps, not knowledge gaps, and they need a different kind of support than reteaching content.

sections.title: Structuring an Ongoing Mentorship Relationship
learningObjectives: Understand the general shape of a mentorship relationship over time
Recognize why a single observed session isn't the same as mentorship
sections.content: Mentorship extends beyond the observed delivery assessment (L5-M6) into an ongoing relationship - periodic check-ins, availability for questions as a new instructor gains experience, and gradually reduced oversight as confidence builds. Specific program structure and cadence will be confirmed as DiFacto's instructor network scales, but the underlying shape is consistent: support that fades as competence grows, not support that ends at certification.

sections.title: Observing Without Taking Over
learningObjectives: Understand the discipline of observing a mentee's session without interrupting
Recognize when intervention during a live session is genuinely necessary
sections.content: When a mentor sits in on a new instructor's session, the instinct to jump in and fix a stumble can undermine the new instructor's confidence and the learners' sense of who's actually teaching. Mentors generally hold back unless something genuinely incorrect is being taught or a safety issue arises - saving feedback for afterward, applying the same specific, timely feedback principles from L5-M1.

sections.title: Debriefing After a Session
learningObjectives: Understand how to structure a post-session debrief with a mentee
Recognize the value of the mentee self-assessing before receiving mentor feedback
sections.content: An effective debrief starts by asking the new instructor what they thought went well and what they'd adjust - self-assessment first, mentor feedback second. This builds the new instructor's own evaluative judgment over time, rather than creating dependence on external feedback for every session. The mentor's feedback then fills gaps or confirms what the new instructor already noticed.

keyTerms.note: A structured conversation after a session to review what happened and what to adjust.
The learner's own judgment of what went well and what to change, given before feedback.

sections.title: Knowing When Mentorship Is Complete
learningObjectives: Understand general signals that a new instructor is ready for independent delivery
Recognize this module's place leading into the observed delivery assessment
sections.content: Mentorship isn't indefinite - it tapers off as a new instructor demonstrates consistent, independent competence across multiple sessions. Recognizing this point is itself a mentorship skill, distinct from the formal observed delivery assessment that follows in L5-M6, which validates certification-level competency through a single structured observation.

questions.question: Why is mentorship treated as a distinct skill from teaching ability?
options: It covers technical content that new instructors have not yet learned
It is only needed when an instructor has failed an assessment and must retake it
It is an ongoing, relational skill, unlike delivering one session well
questions.feedback: Correct. Teaching well and mentoring someone else through their own development are different skills.

questions.question: What do new instructors typically struggle with most?
options: The technical material, since they have only just learned it
Understanding the certification path that brought them to L5
questions.feedback: Correct. New instructors typically know the material but need support with instructional execution.

questions.question: What should a mentor generally do during a mentee's live session?
options: Step in quickly whenever the mentee stumbles, so that the learners are never left confused
Hold back unless something incorrect or unsafe is taught, and give feedback afterward
Stay out of the room so the mentee is never observed at all
questions.feedback: Correct. Interrupting unnecessarily can undermine the new instructor's confidence and authority.

questions.question: What should a post-session debrief start with?
options: The mentee's own view of what went well and what to adjust
The mentor's full evaluation, so the mentee knows what to fix
A review of the learners' quiz scores before anything else
questions.feedback: Correct. Starting with self-assessment builds the new instructor's own evaluative judgment.

questions.question: Is mentorship meant to continue indefinitely?
options: Yes, every certified instructor keeps a mentor for their whole career
No, it ends the moment the observed delivery assessment is passed
No, it tapers off as the new instructor shows consistent independent competence
questions.feedback: Correct. Mentorship support fades as competence and confidence build, rather than continuing indefinitely.
